fields.explanation: RESOLUTION. (1) Public reporting. The measure requires an annual published report (Section 54088) with 'detailed information regarding the investments' from the bond, 'pursuant to Section 50408'. Section 54088 itself names no metrics. It ties the report to existing Health and Safety Code 50408, which (as reproduced by HCD) requires the number of units assisted, households served and their incomes, and the distribution of units among areas of the state. For the Multifamily Housing Program, which gets $5.1 billion of the rental money, existing Section 50675.12 also requires that annual report to give the location of projects and units and the average cost per project and cost per unit. So the report must cover numbers and general locations of assisted homes, and per-unit cost for the main rental program. It is not a measure-specific list of every home. LAO says nothing about reporting. (2) Targets. Neither the statute nor LAO sets any target for homes built or for cost per home. LAO's 40,000 figures are 'up to' estimates. The only numeric unit rule is that at least 10 percent of assisted units in each funded development must be affordable to extremely low income households. That is an affordability mix, not a production target. (3) CalVet review. The independent accountant survey covers the financial condition of CalVet's Division of Farm and Home Purchases while the bonds are outstanding. It goes to CalVet, the Veterans Board, legislative committees and the finance committee. It is not described as public, and it is a review of the loan program's finances, not of the bond spending itself. (4) No State Auditor or other audit of the $10 billion housing money appears in the measure text. Our current text is accurate on targets but understates what the annual report must contain and slightly mislabels the CalVet review.
fields.proposedText: An annual public report on the bond. Under existing law it must show homes assisted, households served and where the homes are, and for the main rental program, cost per unit. A yearly independent accountant review of CalVet's home loan finances. No target for homes built or cost per home.
fields.limitations: Sections 50408 and 50675.12 were read as reproduced in HCD's 2023-24 annual report, not from the codes directly (leginfo was not reachable through the tool). They could have been amended since. 'Administering entity' is not defined in the measure (reader found no definition), so which agency publishes is unclear. 50675.12 cost-per-unit reporting applies only to the Multifamily Housing Program share, not to the $2.1 billion preservation money, homeownership, farmworker, tribal, student or infrastructure money. Student housing money must meet Education Code 17201(i) and (o) reporting rules, which were not read.

conflicts: The official argument in favor says 'Voters will be able to see exactly how many homes get built, where, and at what cost.' Section 54088 lists no metrics itself. Existing law (50408, 50675.12 as reproduced by HCD) requires units assisted and their distribution, and cost per unit only for the Multifamily Housing Program. Location detail is 'distribution among various areas' for all programs, and 'location and geographical distribution' for MHP.

The bill caption on legiplex and the calmatters digest page reads 'The Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026'. The chaptered text's short title (Section 54050) is 'Veterans and Affordable Housing Bond Act of 2026'.
